case_name: Sri Mritunjoy Pathak vs Smt. Kakali Pathak
facts_of_case: The husband complains of the amount directed to be paid on account of alimony pendente lite and litigation expenses on the wife's application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party who fails to produce evidence.
legal_principles.held: Since it is the admitted position that the petitioner's income certificate was not produced before the trial court and the trial court was entitled to draw an adverse inference against the petitioner

outcome.final_order: The order is well-reasoned and deals with the evidence that was before the court in great detail. The order dated September 15, 2014 does not call for any interference, particularly at the behest of the husband.

keywords: Latin maxim: justice delayed is justice denied
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for alimony pendente lite
responding to an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act
drafting a reply to a well-reasoned order
